t.7.64.1: Having sent Śatrughna on his way, Rāghava, together with his two brothers, rejoiced in happiness, protecting the kingdom in accordance with dharma.
t.7.64.2: Then, after a few days, an aged brahmin from the countryside came to the gate of the king's palace, carrying the dead body of a boy.
t.7.64.4: What evil deed did I commit before, in another body, that I now see you, my only son, gone to death?
t.7.64.3: Weeping, he poured out many kinds of words filled with tender affection, and crying again and again, "O son, O son!", he spoke these words.
t.7.64.5: O my little son, a mere boy of five years who had not yet reached youth, you have met death before your time, to my sorrow.
t.7.64.6: Within a few days I shall go to my death, there is no doubt of it, I and your mother too, through grief for you, dear little son.
t.7.64.7: I do not recall ever having spoken a falsehood, nor do I recall having done any harm. For what misdeed of mine has my son, a mere child, been led today to the abode of Vaivasvata without having performed the rites due to his father?
t.7.64.8: Never before have I seen or heard of anything so terrible to behold as this: the death of those whose time has not yet come, here in the realm of Rāma.
t.7.64.9: There is some great misdeed on the part of Rāma, of that there is no doubt. O King, you must bring back to life this boy who has fallen into the power of death.
t.7.64.10: O king, together with your brothers may you attain a long life! O mighty one, we have dwelt happily in this kingdom of yours.
t.7.64.11: Now the realm of the great-souled Ikṣvākus is without a protector, for here it has gained as its lord Rāma, a king who brings about the death of children.
t.7.64.12: Through the faults of the king, subjects who are not governed according to rule fall into ruin; and when the ruler is of wicked conduct, people die before their time.
t.7.64.13: When people in the cities and in the countryside do what is improper, and there is no protection, then arises fear caused by untimely death.
t.7.64.14: Clearly this will be the king's fault, there is no doubt, for this death of a child has then come about in the city or in the countryside.
t.7.64.15: Thus, reproaching the king again and again with words of many kinds, he, burning with grief, clasped that son of his in his arms.
